# Transfer retry panel with decoded progress

This workspace selects files, starts transfers, records queue and progress
history, and paints progress for the open panel. Run it with Node v16.20.2; it
has no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports the workspace and the source
helpers used by the host application.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit.
The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise.

`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel.
The queue adapter in `src/queue.js` shows how those two outputs currently relate
to a visit. Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup
retain their existing behavior. Queue records remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` unless a separate authorization adds
`byteCount` from `file.size`.

The same feed API also has a diagnostic consumer in `src/telemetry.js`.
It is not the panel and must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired. `src/progress-source.js` is the host-visible feed implementation;
the navigation and transfer modules show how ownership is handed off when a
listener is released. Host callbacks are synchronous unless their code returns
a Promise.

messages.text: I’ll trace the candidate transfer and progress code, then make the smallest change that restores the initial frame and keeps the displayed full frame from moving backward. I’ll run the visible checks afterward.

The feed emits its cached packet synchronously from `start()`, but the panel listener is currently added afterward. I’ll attach the panel listener first and keep the diagnostic consumer’s start order unchanged. I’ll also number packets when they arrive so late decoding cannot repaint an older full frame; history will still receive every decoded frame.

My first smoke check failed because I attached telemetry to the same feed before the panel started. In that setup, telemetry correctly sees the panel’s start event. I’m adjusting the check to test telemetry’s own startup separately, then I’ll rerun the ordering and reuse cases.

Updated [src/progress.js](/workspace/src/progress.js) so the panel listener receives a synchronously emitted initial packet. Decoded frames still enter progress history, while an older frame that finishes decoding late can no longer move the display backward.

A Node smoke check passed for the initial update, reversed decode order, history, telemetry startup, and selecting the same file again. Git diff checks were unavailable because this workspace is not a Git repository.

                          show context between diff hunks up to the specified number of lines
    --output-indicator-new <char>
                          specify the character to indicate a new line instead of '+'
    --output-indicator-old <char>
                          specify the character to indicate an old line instead of '-'
    --output-indicator-context <char>
                          specify the character to indicate a context instead of ' '

Diff rename options
    -B, --break-rewrites[=<n>[/<m>]]
                          break complete rewrite changes into pairs of delete and create
    -M, --find-renames[=<n>]
                          detect renames
    -D, --irreversible-delete
                          omit the preimage for deletes
    -C, --find-copies[=<n>]
                          detect copies
    --find-copies-harder  use unmodified files as source to find copies
    --no-renames          disable rename detection
    --rename-empty        use empty blobs as rename source
    --follow              continue listing the history of a file beyond renames
    -l <n>                prevent rename/copy detection if the number of rename/copy targets exceeds given limit

Diff algorithm options
    --minimal             produce the smallest possible diff
    -w, --ignore-all-space
                          ignore whitespace when comparing lines
    -b, --ignore-space-change
                          ignore changes in amount of whitespace
    --ignore-space-at-eol
                          ignore changes in whitespace at EOL
    --ignore-cr-at-eol    ignore carrier-return at the end of line
    --ignore-blank-lines  ignore changes whose lines are all blank
    --indent-heuristic    heuristic to shift diff hunk boundaries for easy reading
    --patience            generate diff using the "patience diff" algorithm
    --histogram           generate diff using the "histogram diff" algorithm
    --diff-algorithm <algorithm>
                          choose a diff algorithm
    --anchored <text>     generate diff using the "anchored diff" algorithm
    --word-diff[=<mode>]  show word diff, using <mode> to delimit changed words
    --word-diff-regex <regex>
                          use <regex> to decide what a word is
    --color-words[=<regex>]
                          equivalent to --word-diff=color --word-diff-regex=<regex>
    --color-moved[=<mode>]
                          moved lines of code are colored differently
    --color-moved-ws <mode>
                          how white spaces are ignored in --color-moved

Other diff options
    --relative[=<prefix>]
                          when run from subdir, exclude changes outside and show relative paths
    -a, --text            treat all files as text
    -R                    swap two inputs, reverse the diff
    --exit-code           exit with 1 if there were differences, 0 otherwise
    --quiet               disable all output of the program
    --ext-diff            allow an external diff helper to be executed
    --textconv            run external text conversion filters when comparing binary files
    --ignore-submodules[=<when>]
                          ignore changes to submodules in the diff generation
    --submodule[=<format>]
                          specify how differences in submodules are shown
    --ita-invisible-in-index
                          hide 'git add -N' entries from the index
    --ita-visible-in-index
                          treat 'git add -N' entries as real in the index
    -S <string>           look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified string
    -G <regex>            look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified regex
    --pickaxe-all         show all changes in the changeset with -S or -G
    --pickaxe-regex       treat <string> in -S as extended POSIX regular expression
    -O <file>             control the order in which files appear in the output
    --find-object <object-id>
                          look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified object
    --diff-filter [(A|C|D|M|R|T|U|X|B)...[*]]
                          select files by diff type
    --output <file>       Output to a specific file
